observations.caveat: Use GHGP table1A as primary baseline. Management criteria have distinct treatment for fuel certificates, aviation effects and downstream renewable electricity. Difference 831,000 tonnes is not an additional physical reduction opportunity. Cat6 gross under management criteria is 276,000, versus GHGP 239,000; do not treat every difference as a certificate subtraction. Crucially p16: management Category11 uses all active Surface/Xbox devices during FY25 (annual telemetry and extrapolation), while GHGP Category11 estimates lifetime use of devices sold in FY25. Third-party devices running Microsoft software are excluded in both. Thus totals differ in service cohort/time boundary, not just renewable procurement.

candidate_intervention_inputs.boundary: Direct control; maintain FY25 service and reliability

candidate_intervention_inputs.overlap: Reduce demand first, then apply alternative clean-supply factor only to remaining load. Do not count both Scope2 accounting alternatives.

candidate_intervention_inputs.intervention: Lower embodied hardware and construction emissions
needed: tonnes concrete/steel and number/chip type servers
replacement required to maintain baseline service
component LCAs and supplier retrofit feasibility
candidate_intervention_inputs.overlap: Capital expenditure in growth year is not the replacement capital needed for fixed 2031 service; no blanket percent reduction to entire category.
Cooling retrofit and refrigerant replacement can affect same emissions and energy.
Product use inventory is lifetime cohort estimate; do not compare directly with annual cloud electricity or subtract renewable certificates twice.

missing_data: Public fleet service denominator: delivered compute, storage, inference/training and network service volume by hardware and site, rather than revenue.
Site IT energy, PUE, cooling process consumption/withdrawal, hourly utilization and weather, temperatures and retrofit compatibility; owned-versus-leased split.
Supplier/site product volumes and bill of materials; disaggregate capital goods into servers, semiconductors, buildings/concrete/steel; embodied emissions, replacement ages and useful lives.
Hourly geographic energy demand/generation matching, marginal emission factors and grid/connection constraints, existing contracted supply and retirement plans.
Basin and monthly water consumption, actual municipal source mix, discharge quality/temperature and ecological response factors; primary-meter coverage and uncertainty intervals.
Waste construction/deconstruction mass, composition, treatment destinations and actual displacement from reuse/recycling.
Species of refrigerants, equipment charge/leak rates and service/retrofit constraints; diesel generator duty hours and standby reliability constraints.
Physical sold-product units by model, lifetime, use patterns and regional grids to separate real use-efficiency improvement from downstream certificate accounting.

valuation_rules: GHG inventory is not synonymous with marginal causal emissions or monetized damages.
Carbon/water/waste remain separate; any dollar damage aggregation requires explicit valuation and uncertainty.
No credit for disclosure quality; missing data is an estimation limit, not evidence of high or low damage.
Financial savings and environmental damage valuations must remain separate.
